newsitem.title: USA: American, BA expect word from British govt soon.
newsitem.headline: American, BA expect word from British govt soon.

text.p: Officials at American Airlines and British Airways expect to receive word from the new British government within the next couple weeks if it will consider the proposed alliance of the two carriers, American President Donald Carty said Tuesday.

"We hope over the next week or two to get some clear direction as to whether or not the British government politically is willing to invest energy getting the deal approved and whether they're happy with the deal in its current form," Carty said at a luncheon.
Carty said the position of the newly elected British government toward the proposed alliance was still not clear.
"The precise attitude of the incoming British government to our deal remains a little bit of an uncertainty," Carty said.

Carty said the alliance can not afford to give up a large amount of its slots at London's Heathrow Airport in order to soften competition concerns and to quicken the pace of the approval. He said giving up slots would cut the profits of the pact, making it undesirable.
"We're not going to enter into an agreement that nullifies all the economic advantages," Carty said.
American is a unit of AMR Corp.
